hidden_case.analysis: evaluate_deletion() computes 'referenced' via plain string-set membership on Path(...).as_posix() without any path resolution/canonicalization. When the pointer path and the candidate path are equivalent but differ in absolute/relative form (an extremely common, foreseeable real-world condition -- pointer files commonly store one path convention while a caller's cwd or deletion tooling uses another), the guard silently concludes the file is NOT referenced and ALLOWS deletion of a genuinely unique, genuinely depended-upon file. This is a direct, severe violation of the guard's own core purpose: it fails OPEN exactly where the falsifiable hypothesis requires it to fail closed, and the failure mode is squarely within the literal scope of the stated hypothesis (a truly unique file, truly referenced by a current pointer).
